requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.fingerprints` has no implementation roots and no Implements edges. Each clause specifies observable behavior, not how the code is built.

- "Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words": this fixes the digest value. An implementation using another algorithm would produce different hashes, so that would break observable behavior. Which library computes SHA-256 is discretionary. The encoding rules themselves belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which is context here.
- "The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version": this is the value the scheme reports. The `fingerprint_scheme` signature and the retention of the scheme in loaded contents are stated in the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, which is context here.
- "Comments are excluded from structural hashes": this is the result for a given input. A different way of excluding comments, such as filtering tokens or nodes, gives the same hashes.

So no structural obligation needs implementation evidence here, and nothing is missing.

behavioral: The tests adequately cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.fingerprints`.

**Obligations**
1. Structural hashes are SHA-256 over the structural encoding of whitespace-separated words, as `requirements.references.structural_hash` defines them.
2. Comments are excluded from the hash.
3. The fingerprint scheme identifies the TOML rules and their version, as `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` defines it.

The cited requirements are context only. I did not reassess their implementation or tests.

**Coverage**
- **SHA-256 digest:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` asserts that the TOML fingerprint is 64 hex characters. That alone would accept any 256-bit hash. The shared encoder is tested against known SHA-256 vectors in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. It checks the empty-input digest and a tagged, length-prefixed text token. The requirement says the same rule applies in every language, so that test covers the TOML digest too.
- **Whitespace and word boundaries:** The same test uses a TOML case `[t]\n# note\na = "two words"`. It asserts that the hash is unchanged when the spacing becomes `"two   words"` and the comment text changes. It asserts that `"twowords"` gives a different hash. That checks that whitespace is not hashed and that each word is encoded separately.
- **Comments excluded:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a TOML case with `table[t]`.
  - Changing the text of a leading comment and a trailing comment leaves the hash equal.
  - Removing the comments entirely leaves the hash equal.
  - Changing the non-comment value `1` to `2` makes the hash differ, so the comparison is not vacuous.
- **Scheme:** The `check` helper in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` is called with `languages::Toml`. It asserts `fingerprint_scheme()` equals `toml-structural-v1`, both from the language and from `Default`. It asserts that loaded `OutlineContent` retains that scheme. It also asserts a successful `table[check]` selection and an equal fingerprint across upper-case extensions.

The requirement that a rule change uses a new scheme is a maintenance convention. It has no independently observable behaviour to test here.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. No unacknowledged gap remains.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
